title: Levers and Lifting
description: Recognize a lever’s parts through a supported bar, a turning point, and the forces used to move a load.
cardDescription: Recognize a lever’s parts through a supported bar, a turning point, and the forces used to move a load.
focus: A lever turns around a support. Its geometry can trade a greater movement distance for a smaller required force, but it does not create energy or eliminate the work of lifting.
solvingTip: Look for the part’s role: turning point, applied force, or object being moved. Several ordinary words have precise meanings in this scene.
words: Rigid bar turning about a support to move a load
Support or turning point about which a lever rotates
Object or resistance moved by a simple machine
Applied input force used to operate a simple machine
Lever ___, perpendicular distance from a pivot to a force's line of action
Point about which a rigid object turns
Long rigid piece used as a simple levering tool
Long structural member supported in a balance
To move something using a levering action
To raise a load to a higher position
To bring opposing turning effects into equilibrium
Weighing instrument that may use a balanced beam
Specific location at which a force is applied
Push or pull acting on an object

answerNotes.LEVER: A lever rotates around a fulcrum. The distances from that support determine how its forces and movements relate.
answerNotes.FULCRUM: The fulcrum is the pivot support. It is different from the load being moved or the effort applied by the user.
answerNotes.LOAD: Load names what is being acted on. Effort names the applied force used to act on it.
answerNotes.EFFORT: Effort is an input force. A machine may reduce the force needed by increasing the distance over which that force acts.
answerNotes.ARM: The effective lever arm is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force's line of action. It need not equal the full length of the bar.

title: A Pulley and a Rope
description: Follow a rope around a grooved wheel and distinguish the names for the support, moving load, and lifting arrangement.
cardDescription: Follow a rope around a grooved wheel and distinguish the names for the support, moving load, and lifting arrangement.
focus: A pulley can change a force’s direction, and a multiple-pulley arrangement can change the force needed. The number of supporting rope sections matters more than simply counting visible wheels.
solvingTip: Separate the wheel itself from the whole arrangement. The short rope and support words can provide crossings for the technical term.
words: Grooved wheel over which a rope runs to transmit a pulling force
Grooved wheel within a pulley block
Rope-and-pulley arrangement used together for lifting
Channel around a pulley wheel that guides a rope
Central shaft supporting a rotating pulley wheel
Flexible line running around a pulley wheel
Weight or object raised by the lifting arrangement
To raise an object with a rope system
Curved attachment holding a suspended load
Frame containing one or more pulley wheels
Thin flexible line usable with a small pulley
Round rotating part of the mechanism
To rotate as a rope moves around the rim
Downward gravitational force acting on a suspended object

answerNotes.PULLEY: A single fixed pulley mainly changes the direction of pulling. Arrangements with moving pulleys can also provide a force advantage.
answerNotes.SHEAVE: Sheave names the wheel. A block may contain one or more sheaves and the frame supporting them.
answerNotes.TACKLE: A block and tackle combines rope and pulley blocks. Its mechanical advantage depends on the way the load is supported.
answerNotes.GROOVE: The groove helps keep the rope on the wheel. It differs from the axle at the center of rotation.
answerNotes.AXLE: The wheel turns around or with an axle, depending on the design. The rope runs at the rim rather than through that central shaft.

title: Wheels and Axles
description: Examine the center, edge, and supporting parts of an ordinary wheel through familiar carts and wagons.
cardDescription: Examine the center, edge, and supporting parts of an ordinary wheel through familiar carts and wagons.
focus: Wheel parts have names based on their position and function. A bearing supports relative motion, while lubrication can reduce friction; neither is simply another name for the axle itself.
solvingTip: Picture the center and the outside edge. A radial part connects them, while a supporting part allows rotation.
words: Shaft supporting or connecting rotating wheels
Central part of a wheel surrounding its axle
Outer circular edge of a wheel
One radial member connecting a wheel's center and outer edge
Component supporting motion between a rotating shaft and its support
Round part that rolls beneath a cart
To move while turning over a surface
Small wheeled vehicle used to carry a load
Four-wheeled carrying vehicle often pulled by a handle or team
Semisolid lubricant used on some moving mechanical parts
Circular in shape, like a wheel
Opening through the center of a component
Cargo or weight supported by a wheeled vehicle

answerNotes.AXLE: An axle supports the wheel arrangement. Depending on the design, the wheel or the axle may rotate relative to the other.
answerNotes.HUB: The hub occupies the center. The rim forms the outside edge, with spokes connecting them in a spoked wheel.
answerNotes.RIM: The rim is at the circumference. It is distinct from the central hub and the axle passing through the center.
answerNotes.SPOKE: A spoke runs outward from the hub toward the rim. Not all wheels use separate spokes.
answerNotes.BEARING: A bearing permits controlled relative movement. Designs can use rolling elements or sliding surfaces.

title: Gears at Work
description: Identify toothed wheels and the words describing how they transfer rotation from one shaft to another.
cardDescription: Identify toothed wheels and the words describing how they transfer rotation from one shaft to another.
focus: Gear size and arrangement affect speed, direction, and turning force. Directly meshing external gears turn in opposite directions, but not every gear system follows that same simple layout.
solvingTip: Watch singular and plural forms. A component name differs from a relationship such as speed ratio or from the turning effect called torque.
words: Smaller gear in a meshing pair
Intermediate gear used between driving and driven gears
Turning effect of a force about an axis
Type of gear with teeth on a conical surface
To engage so that one gear's teeth fit between another's
Toothed wheel used to transmit rotary motion
One projecting element on the edge of a gear
Plural name for a gear's projecting elements
Numerical relationship between two gear tooth counts
Long rotating rod carrying a gear
To supply motion to another mechanical part
Rate at which a rotating gear turns
To move around a central axis

answerNotes.PINION: Pinion commonly names the smaller member of a gear pair. Its tooth count helps determine the speed relationship.
answerNotes.IDLER: An idler can alter direction or spacing. In a simple gear train it does not independently change the overall tooth-count ratio between the first and last gears.
answerNotes.TORQUE: Torque is a turning effect. It differs from rotational speed, even though a gear system relates the two through power transfer.
answerNotes.BEVEL: Bevel gears transmit rotation between intersecting shaft axes. Their shape differs from ordinary cylindrical spur gears.
answerNotes.MESH: Meshing allows teeth to transfer motion. Two directly meshing external gears rotate in opposite directions.

title: Ramps and Screws
description: Compare inclined surfaces and spiral threads through the everyday vocabulary of simple machines.
cardDescription: Compare inclined surfaces and spiral threads through the everyday vocabulary of simple machines.
focus: A ramp trades distance for the force needed to raise a load. A screw uses an inclined path wrapped around a shaft, while a wedge applies force through sloping surfaces.
solvingTip: Look at the shape and the motion. A straight incline, a spiral ridge, and a tapered splitting shape require different names.
words: Sloping surface connecting two different heights
Fastener or machine with a helical ridge around a shaft
Helical ridge around a screw or inside a matching nut
Tapered tool whose sloping sides separate or lift material
Winding path suggested by a screw's thread
Surface that rises at an angle rather than staying level
Vertical height gained along a ramp
Horizontal distance associated with a slope
To rotate a screw around its axis
Threaded fastener commonly paired with a nut
Internally threaded piece fitted onto a bolt
Tapered tip at the end of many screws
Push or pull applied to move a load along a ramp

answerNotes.RAMP: A ramp allows a load to rise over a longer path. Ideally this reduces the needed force while increasing the distance traveled.
answerNotes.SCREW: A screw's thread follows a spiral path around its shaft. Rotation can produce forward motion when the thread engages a matching surface.
answerNotes.THREAD: Thread names the ridge and groove system. It has a mechanical meaning here rather than meaning sewing fiber.
answerNotes.WEDGE: A wedge uses inclined surfaces to redirect force. It differs from a ramp that remains stationary while a load travels over it.
answerNotes.SPIRAL: A screw thread is a three-dimensional helix. Spiral is the familiar everyday description used in this clue.
